# Higgs Decays into Right-Handed Neutrinos via Higher-Dimension Operators

Certain TeV-suppressed higher-dimension operators can open new decay channels that allow the Higgs boson to decay into lighter right-handed neutrinos. These operators, which arise naturally in extensions of the Standard Model featuring new physics at the TeV scale, provide a coupling between the Higgs sector and the right-handed neutrino states that would otherwise be absent in the minimal framework.

The phenomenological impact of these new decay channels depends sensitively on the mass of the Higgs boson. When the Higgs boson is light, these channels may dominate over all other decay modes, fundamentally altering the expected branching ratios and search strategies. For Higgs masses larger than $2m_W$, where decays into a pair of $W$ bosons become kinematically accessible, the new channels become subdominant. Nevertheless, they remain phenomenologically relevant and can still provide observable signatures.

A key feature of this scenario lies in the properties of the right-handed neutrinos themselves. These particles possess macroscopic decay lengths, meaning they travel a measurable distance before decaying. Their decays proceed predominantly into final states containing both leptons and quarks, giving rise to characteristic multi-particle signatures within the detector volume.

The resulting collider signature is particularly distinctive: a pair of displaced vertices that violate lepton number. The displaced nature of these vertices, arising from the long lifetime of the right-handed neutrinos, combined with the violation of lepton number conservation, offers a clean and identifiable experimental handle. Such signatures are relatively free from Standard Model backgrounds, making them especially promising for discovery.

To assess the viability of this scenario, the analysis employs the minimal flavor violation hypothesis. Within this framework, the decays can occur consistently with existing experimental constraints, demonstrating that the proposed mechanism does not conflict with current bounds. Crucially, the extent to which these decay channels dominate depends on the approximate flavor symmetries of the right-handed neutrinos, which govern the structure of their couplings and thereby determine the relative importance of the new decay modes.

# Higgs Decays to Right-Handed Neutrinos via Higher-Dimension Operators

## Introduction and Motivation

The discovery of neutrino masses stands as one of the clearest indications of physics beyond the Standard Model. A particularly compelling framework for generating these masses involves the introduction of right-handed neutrinos, which are singlets under the Standard Model gauge group. If these right-handed neutrinos are relatively light, they may participate in the phenomenology accessible at collider experiments, opening up novel channels through which the properties of both neutrinos and the Higgs sector can be probed.

In this work, we explore the possibility that the Higgs boson may decay into these lighter right-handed neutrinos through the influence of higher-dimension operators. Such operators, suppressed by a characteristic mass scale of order a TeV, can arise naturally when heavier degrees of freedom are integrated out from a more complete underlying theory. When these operators are present, they can mediate Higgs decay modes that would otherwise be absent or highly suppressed in the minimal renormalizable framework, thereby providing a window into new physics at the electroweak scale and beyond.

## General Operator Analysis and Flavor Structure

To investigate this scenario systematically, we adopt a general operator analysis that catalogs the possible higher-dimension interactions consistent with the symmetries of the theory. A central challenge in any such construction is the tension between introducing new interactions involving the lepton sector and the stringent experimental bounds on processes that violate lepton number. Observations of phenomena such as neutrinoless double beta decay and various rare lepton-flavor-violating transitions place severe constraints on the allowed strength and structure of these operators.

To remain consistent with these experimental limits while retaining predictive power, we employ the hypothesis of minimal flavor violation. Under this assumption, the only sources of flavor and lepton number breaking are those already present in the Standard Model Yukawa couplings, extended appropriately to include the neutrino sector. This organizing principle allows us to construct operators whose contributions to dangerous lepton-number-violating observables are naturally suppressed, ensuring that the scenario evades current experimental constraints without requiring artificial fine-tuning of parameters.

## Collider Signatures

The most striking consequence of these novel Higgs decays lies in their distinctive collider phenomenology. When the Higgs boson decays into right-handed neutrinos, the subsequent behavior of these particles can produce a remarkable experimental signature: pairs of displaced vertices that violate lepton number. Because the right-handed neutrinos couple only weakly and may be relatively long-lived, they travel a measurable distance before decaying, giving rise to secondary vertices that are spatially separated from the primary interaction point.

The appearance of two such displaced vertices simultaneously, combined with the violation of lepton number in the decay products, constitutes a signature with very low Standard Model background. This makes the scenario particularly attractive from an experimental standpoint, as the observation of paired displaced vertices with lepton-number-violating final states would provide compelling evidence for the presence of the higher-dimension operators under consideration.

## Role of Approximate Flavor Symmetries

A key finding of our analysis concerns the conditions under which these exotic decay modes come to dominate the Higgs phenomenology. We find that the prominence of these decays depends crucially on the approximate flavor symmetries governing the right-handed neutrino sector. The specific pattern of these symmetries determines the relative sizes of the various operator contributions and, consequently, whether the displaced-vertex signatures are observable at collider experiments.

When the flavor symmetries take particular forms, the decays into right-handed neutrinos can become the dominant exotic mode, yielding an appreciable branching fraction that could be detected in present or future data. Conversely, different symmetry structures can suppress these channels considerably. This sensitivity underscores the deep connection between the flavor structure of the neutrino sector and the collider phenomenology of the Higgs boson, suggesting that measurements of these decay modes could in principle reveal information about the underlying flavor symmetries of nature.

## Conclusion

In summary, we have shown that TeV-suppressed higher-dimension operators offer a viable and phenomenologically rich mechanism for Higgs decays into lighter right-handed neutrinos. By employing the minimal flavor violation hypothesis, this scenario remains consistent with the demanding constraints on lepton-number-violating processes, while predicting a distinctive signature of paired displaced vertices at colliders. The dependence of these decays on the approximate flavor symmetries of the right-handed neutrinos highlights the potential for collider experiments to shed light on the fundamental structure of the neutrino sector and the physics responsible for neutrino masses.

# The TeV Scale and the Higgs Boson

## Introduction

The discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 stands as one of the most significant achievements in modern physics, confirming a theoretical prediction made nearly half a century earlier. Central to this discovery was the ability of particle accelerators to reach energies at the **TeV (tera-electron-volt) scale**, a threshold that opened new windows into the fundamental structure of matter.

## Understanding the TeV Scale

The electron-volt (eV) is a unit of energy commonly used in particle physics. A **tera-electron-volt (TeV)** represents one trillion (10¹²) electron-volts—an enormous concentration of energy at the subatomic level. The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN operates in this regime, colliding protons at energies of several TeV to recreate conditions similar to those that existed fractions of a second after the Big Bang.

Reaching TeV energies was essential because the Higgs boson is a massive particle, weighing approximately 125 GeV (0.125 TeV). Producing such particles requires collisions energetic enough to convert kinetic energy into mass, following Einstein's famous relation, E = mc².

## The Role of the Higgs Boson

The **Higgs boson** is a manifestation of the Higgs field, an invisible energy field that permeates the entire universe. According to the Standard Model of particle physics, particles acquire mass through their interaction with this field. Without the Higgs mechanism, fundamental particles like electrons and quarks would remain massless, and the universe as we know it—with atoms, stars, and life—could not exist.

## Significance of the Discovery

The confirmation of the Higgs boson at the TeV scale:

- **Validated the Standard Model**, completing its roster of predicted particles.
- **Explained the origin of mass** for elementary particles.
- **Opened new research directions**, including investigations into physics beyond the Standard Model, such as dark matter and supersymmetry.

## Conclusion

The interplay between the TeV energy scale and the Higgs boson represents a triumph of both theoretical insight and experimental engineering. As accelerators continue to push toward even higher energies, physicists hope to uncover deeper mysteries of the universe, potentially reshaping our understanding of reality itself.

In extensions of the Standard Model that incorporate right-handed neutrinos to explain the origin of neutrino masses, additional interactions between the Higgs sector and the sterile neutrino states can arise from physics at a high energy scale Λ. We compute the partial decay width for the process h → NN and, for right-handed neutrinos that mix with the active sector, the decay h → νN, as functions of the effective operator coefficients and the new physics scale. For right-handed neutrino masses in the GeV to electroweak range, we find that these exotic Higgs decays can yield distinctive experimental signatures, including displaced vertices and same-sign lepton pairs arising from the subsequent decay of the long-lived Majorana neutrinos. We derive constraints on the relevant Wilson coefficients from current LHC measurements of the Higgs invisible and exotic branching ratios, and assess the discovery potential at the High-Luminosity LHC and proposed future colliders.

Our results demonstrate that Higgs boson decays provide a sensitive and complementary probe of the neutrino mass generation mechanism, potentially accessing regions of parameter space beyond the reach of direct production searches for heavy neutral leptons. We discuss the implications of our findings for leptogenesis and the broader landscape of models addressing the neutrino mass hierarchy.

**Lepton-Number-Violating Higgs Decays in the Minimal Flavor Violation Framework: New Signatures at Colliders**

We investigate novel decay channels of the Standard Model Higgs boson arising from lepton number violation (LNV) within an effective field theory constrained by the principle of Minimal Flavor Violation (MFV). By extending the MFV hypothesis to the leptonic sector through the inclusion of right-handed neutrino Yukawa couplings and Majorana mass terms, we construct a complete basis of dimension-six and dimension-seven operators that mediate exotic Higgs decays while remaining consistent with stringent constraints from charged lepton flavor violation and neutrinoless double beta decay.

We demonstrate that the spurion analysis characteristic of MFV naturally suppresses dangerous flavor-violating contributions, allowing for phenomenologically viable branching ratios in channels such as $h \to \ell^\pm \ell^\pm jj$ and $h \to \ell^\pm W^\mp$, where the same-sign dilepton final states provide unambiguous signatures of $\Delta L = 2$ processes. The interplay between the MFV flavor structure and the seesaw mechanism yields predictive relations among the decay rates into different lepton flavors, governed by the light neutrino mass matrix and mixing parameters.

Working at leading order in the MFV expansion, we compute the relevant partial widths and show that for effective operator scales in the range $\Lambda \sim 1$–$10$ TeV, the branching ratios can reach $\mathcal{O}(10^{-4})$–$\mathcal{O}(10^{-6})$, placing them within reach of the high-luminosity LHC and future lepton colliders. We perform a detailed collider analysis of the same-sign dilepton signature, including dominant Standard Model backgrounds from $t\bar{t}$ and diboson production, and estimate the discovery reach as a function of integrated luminosity. Our results establish LNV Higgs decays as a sensitive probe of the flavor structure underlying neutrino mass generation, offering a complementary window to traditional searches at the energy and intensity frontiers.

**Higher-Dimension Operators and Exotic Higgs Decays to Light Right-Handed Neutrinos: Phenomenology and Collider Signatures**

We investigate novel Higgs boson decay channels into light right-handed (sterile) neutrinos generated by higher-dimension operators within an effective field theory (EFT) framework extending the Standard Model. Assuming right-handed neutrinos with masses below the electroweak scale, we systematically classify the dimension-six operators that couple the Higgs doublet to singlet fermions and analyze their contributions to the Higgs decay width. In particular, we focus on operators of the form $(H^\dagger H)(\bar{L}\tilde{H}N)$ and derivative couplings that induce effective $h\to N\nu$ and $h\to NN$ vertices, which are otherwise suppressed by the tiny Yukawa couplings responsible for light neutrino masses in the minimal seesaw mechanism.

# Abstract

We investigate the production of right-handed neutrinos through exotic Higgs boson decays within the framework of Minimal Flavor Violation (MFV). In this scenario, the couplings between the Standard Model and the right-handed neutrino sector are governed by the same flavor symmetry structure that controls the charged lepton and neutrino Yukawa interactions, providing a predictive and theoretically motivated pattern of mixings. We show that MFV naturally accommodates right-handed neutrinos with masses at the GeV-to-electroweak scale and suppressed active-sterile mixing angles, leading to macroscopic decay lengths. Consequently, Higgs decays into right-handed neutrinos can produce displaced vertices observable at the LHC and proposed far-detector experiments. We characterize the resulting signatures, including displaced leptons and jets, and derive the expected sensitivity as a function of the right-handed neutrino mass and the MFV expansion parameters. Our results demonstrate that displaced-vertex searches offer a powerful and complementary probe of the neutrino mass generation mechanism, capable of testing regions of parameter space inaccessible to prompt searches and precision electroweak observables.
